title: RC and RL transients
goal: Drive an RC and an RL circuit with a square wave and measure the time constant two ways on the oscilloscope.
theory: A capacitor charging through R from a step follows v(t) = V·(1 − e^(−t/τ)) with τ = RC; an inductor's current (and the resistor voltage) rises the same way with τ = L/R, while the inductor's own voltage decays as V·e^(−t/τ).

After one τ the response has covered 63.2 % of its change. Way 1: put the scope cursors on the start of the edge and on the 63 % level and read Δt. Way 2: measure the 10 %–90 % rise time t_r, which equals τ·ln 9 ≈ 2.2·τ.
The generator's own 50 Ω output resistance is in series with your resistor — include it when the resistor is small.

prelab.label: τ of 0.5 H with 1 kΩ + 50 Ω

procedure: Load the reference build. The generator gives a 0–5 V square wave at 10 Hz (amplitude 5 Vpp, offset 2.5 V).
Scope CH1 on the generator (c10), CH2 on the capacitor (c16), ground clip on the rail. Set 5 ms/div, trigger on CH1 rising.
Way 1: place cursor A at the edge and cursor B where CH2 reaches 63 % of 5 V; record Δt.
Way 2: read the automatic rise-time measurement on CH2 and divide by 2.2.
Move CH2 to the inductor (a24) and repeat at 0.5 ms/div for the RL circuit.

checks.label: Inductor voltage decays with τ = L/(R + 50 Ω)
